original_question: Does every Jordan curve in the plane contain four points that are the vertices of a square? Here a Jordan curve is a simple closed curve, and 'inscribes a square' means that the four vertices of the square lie on the curve, without requiring the whole square to lie inside the region bounded by the curve.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s official formulation: it asks the same existence question for any Jordan curve in the plane, and it correctly includes the paper’s clarification that “inscribes a square” means only that the four vertices of the square lie on the curve, not that the whole square must lie in the bounded interior region. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/abs/2104.09324))
missing_details: The paper defines a Jordan curve as a parametrized plane curve that is closed and simple, so the continuity/parametrization viewpoint is implicit in the official setup even though your draft compresses this to “simple closed curve.” ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/abs/2104.09324))

To be maximally faithful to the paper, the quantifier should be understood as completely unrestricted: the problem concerns arbitrary Jordan curves, with no extra assumptions such as convexity, polygonality, smoothness, analyticity, rectifiability, symmetry, or local monotonicity. The nearby context explicitly says many such special families are already settled, while the general Jordan-curve case remains open. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/abs/2104.09324))

The official wording is “Decide if any Jordan curve inscribes a square,” so the target is a pure yes/no existence problem; it is not asking for the number of squares, uniqueness, or containment of the square in the interior. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/abs/2104.09324))
refined_question: Does every Jordan curve in the Euclidean plane \(\mathbb{R}^2\)—that is, every closed simple parametrized plane curve—inscribe a square? Equivalently, must there exist four points on the curve that are the vertices of a square, without requiring the square itself to be contained in the bounded component of the complement of the curve? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/abs/2104.09324))
justification: The nearest official target is exactly Problem 6 in Section 6, not a broader neighboring question about inscribed polygons or special curve classes. Your draft already captures the main statement almost verbatim, so the only necessary refinements are to align “Jordan curve” with the paper’s closed-and-simple parametrized-curve setup and to make explicit that no regularity assumptions beyond being a Jordan curve are intended. I did not broaden the question to rectangles, rhombi, or convex curves, because the paper mentions those only as surrounding context and solved special cases, not as the main open problem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/abs/2104.09324))
